summary.intent: Prepare hackathon (neathack) submission materials for Crashtest, and respond to neatlogs' engineering lead Akshay's request by running Crashtest against the neatroots repo and producing a verified findings report.
summary.outcome: Fixed a shell-filter gap for agent-written cleanup commands (pkill) and re-shot clean X images. Started the neatroots analysis, found and fixed a Crashtest bug where pending-question buttons died after an app restart, and committed and pushed it (src/main/agent/orchestrator.ts). The P1 run on AWS and the report to Akshay are still pending.

repo: Crashtest's orchestrator asks the user to choose when a repo contains multiple products; the pending choice was held in memory only, so after an app restart the buttons did nothing.
Agent-written post-setup cleanup commands (e.g. `pkill -f 'node index.js'`) bypassed the shell safety filter and could kill unrelated processes on the host; they now go through the same filter.
E2E runs can leave orphaned vite processes; check for leftover processes after each scenario run.
The AWS EC2 server has only 1 GB RAM; a 4 GB swap file was added so it can build neatroots.
Untrusted repo setup scripts can touch paths such as ~/.claude, so unknown repos are run on the AWS server rather than the user's Mac.

code.finding: Product-choice state was made to survive app restarts. Clicking a stale button now resumes the analysis. Other stale question types show a restart message instead of failing silently.

workflow: Verify fixes by reproducing the original failure, e.g. clicking the same dead button again after the fix.
Use Playwright to take clean screenshots after dismissing login and cookie overlays.
Use a background Monitor to track long-running analysis progress instead of polling.
Verify every bug found in third-party code against the source before reporting it, since the recipient owns the code.

friction: The earlier X screenshots had a login box and a cookie banner overlaid and had to be re-shot.
The user asked 'niye durdun' (why did you stop) because the neatroots analysis was stalled on the dead product-choice button and looked like inactivity.
Leftover vite processes from an earlier run were still alive and had to be killed by hand.
The 1 GB RAM on the server was a build constraint and needed a swap workaround.
open_items: Run the neatroots P1 scenarios on the AWS server once scenario writing finishes.
Verify each found bug in the neatroots source and prepare a clean report and reply tweet for Akshay.
The user still has to post Post 3, join the 09:30 AMA, and send proof that the cfo.ai subscription was cancelled.
Post 4 (cfo.ai) and Post 4b (Entire) are scheduled for about 13:00 and 18:00 PDT, and 1–2 new posts are planned for day 2.
Possibly adjust the testing focus based on Akshay's answers at the AMA (replay, collector, MCP tools).
